id: Affordances and feedback in interface design.md
title: Affordances and feedback in interface design

schemaData.title: Affordances and feedback in interface design
schemaData.summary: How affordances and feedback together explain why interfaces feel intuitive
schemaData.content: Norman's [[Affordance]] explains how people know what they can do; his feedback principle explains how they know it worked. Nielsen's usability heuristics restate both. Interfaces feel intuitive when both hold, and confusing when either fails: a flat button lacks the affordance, and a silent save lacks the feedback.

linkTargets: Affordances and feedback in interface design

id: Why retrieval beats fine-tuning for fresh knowledge.md
title: Why retrieval beats fine-tuning for fresh knowledge

schemaData.title: Why retrieval beats fine-tuning for fresh knowledge
schemaData.summary: Retrieval keeps answers current; fine-tuning bakes in a snapshot
schemaData.content: Lewis et al. (2020) introduced [[Retrieval-augmented generation]]. Ovadia et al. (2024) found fine-tuning rarely teaches new facts. Vendor guides agree. Together they suggest retrieval for facts that change, and fine-tuning for style and format.

id: Lean and kanban share their roots.md
title: Lean and kanban share their roots

schemaData.title: Lean and kanban share their roots
schemaData.summary: Kanban and lean both come from the Toyota Production System
schemaData.content: The [[Toyota Production System]] used cards to limit work in progress. Anderson adapted this as [[Kanban]] for software, and the Poppendiecks adapted the wider system as lean software development. Both keep the same core idea: limit work in progress to expose waste.

id: Why studies disagree on remote work productivity.md
title: Why studies disagree on remote work productivity

schemaData.title: Why studies disagree on remote work productivity
schemaData.summary: The studies measure different things
schemaData.content: Bloom (2015) found a 13% gain in a call centre; Gibbs (2021) found a loss among IT professionals. Bloom measured calls handled; Gibbs measured output per hour worked. The disagreement comes from what each counts as productivity.
